headline: Cyclone Arnab Makes Landfall in Andhra Pradesh with 180,000 Evacuated as Former Typhoon Champi Drives Extreme Bering Sea Storm Toward Western Alaska
overview: Cyclone Arnab struck India's Andhra Pradesh coast on October 28 as a very severe cyclonic storm, triggering mass evacuations and leaving at least 3 dead. Simultaneously, the remnants of former Typhoon Champi are driving a powerful Bering Sea storm system toward western Alaska, generating seas up to 29 feet and Storm Warnings across the Aleutian Islands. Elsewhere, Indonesia's catastrophic wildfires drew a new humanitarian response, Hawaii remained under a multi-island flood watch, and Kīlauea entered the forecast window for its next lava fountaining episode.

events.title: Cyclone Arnab Makes Landfall in Andhra Pradesh — 180,000 Evacuated, 3 Dead
events.summary: Tropical Cyclone Arnab crossed the Andhra Pradesh–Yanam coast of India on October 28 as a very severe cyclonic storm, marking a rare Bay of Bengal cyclone landfall at a time when El Niño has disrupted typical storm seasons. Indian authorities evacuated more than 180,000 people ahead of landfall, and at least 3 deaths have been confirmed as the storm weakened inland. The National Disaster Response Force was deployed across the affected coastal zone, with heavy rainfall and damaging winds impacting southeastern India.

events.title: Former Typhoon Champi Drives Extreme Bering Sea Storm — Seas Up to 29 Feet, Storm Warnings Across Aleutians
events.location: Western Alaska and Aleutian Islands, USA
events.summary: The remnants of former Typhoon Champi have entered the Bering Sea and are fueling an intense storm system targeting western Alaska, with the National Weather Service issuing Storm Warnings from Adak to Attu along the Aleutian chain. Forecast seas of up to 29 feet and sustained winds of 45–50 knots are expected across the region through October 29, with dangerous conditions on both the Pacific and Bering sides of the Aleutians. Meteorologists note a persistent stormy pattern with little sign of breaking down, compounding impacts alongside the ongoing Brooks Range winter storm.

articles.title: Former Typhoon Champi Takes Aim at Western Alaska with Bering Sea Seas Up to 29 Feet After a Surprise Interior Snowstorm
Stormy weather pattern shows little signs of breaking down for Alaska

events.title: Indonesia Wildfire Crisis Deepens — Oxygen Buses Deployed as Haze Chokes Kalimantan
events.summary: Indonesia's worst wildfire crisis in over a decade continued to intensify on October 28, with the government deploying mobile oxygen buses to aid residents in Palangka Raya, Central Kalimantan, who are suffering acute respiratory distress from choking wildfire haze. The fires, many deliberately set for land clearing and exacerbated by El Niño drought conditions, have already emitted an estimated 14.4 million tonnes of carbon in a single week. Air quality across parts of Borneo and neighboring regions of Southeast Asia remains at hazardous levels, with the humanitarian toll escalating.

articles.title: Indonesia sends oxygen bus to aid residents choking on forest fire haze

events.title: Florida Coastal Flood Warnings Persist — Keys to Northeast Florida and Southeast Georgia
events.location: Florida Keys to Northeast Florida and Coastal Georgia, USA
events.summary: Coastal Flood Warnings remained in effect on October 28 across a broad swath of Florida and southeast Georgia, from the Florida Keys through Miami-Dade, Palm Beach, Brevard, Volusia, Duval, Nassau, and Flagler counties, as well as coastal Glynn and Camden counties in Georgia, with some warnings extended through October 30. Persistent northeast winds and tidal backflow are slowing drainage along the St. Johns River, which is forecast to crest near minor flood stage before beginning a slow decline. Numerous roads face closure risk, and low-lying properties including homes and critical infrastructure are experiencing inundation at high tide.

articles.title: 'Tropical tricks' ahead? Florida faces more gusty winds, coastal flooding

events.title: Hawaii Multi-Island Flood Watch — Tropical Moisture Trough Brings Flash Flood Risk to All Islands
events.location: All Main Hawaiian Islands, Hawaii, USA
events.summary: A Flood Watch remained in effect across all main Hawaiian Islands on October 28 as a slow-moving moisture trough delivered abundant tropical rainfall and isolated thunderstorms, with Oahu and Maui County facing the greatest flash flood risk. The Big Island also saw a High Wind Warning in effect through midday, with summit gusts reaching up to 65 mph. Streams are rising across the state and low-lying areas are at risk of rapid inundation, with conditions expected to gradually improve by October 29.

articles.title: Looming heavy rain prompts flood watch for Hawaii

events.title: Kīlauea Enters Forecast Window for Episode 56 Lava Fountaining
events.summary: Following Episode 55 on October 17, Kīlauea's summit eruption has remained paused as magma chamber inflation gradually resumed, with USGS scientists forecasting that Episode 56 could begin between October 28 and November 5, 2026. Inflationary tilt signals leveled out in recent days but renewed upward trends have been detected, consistent with the pre-fountaining pattern established across previous episodes. The eruption cycle at Halemaʻumaʻu crater continues to be closely monitored, with another dramatic lava fountaining event considered imminent.

events.title: Anomalous Late-October Heat Grips South Asia — Mumbai 35.6°C, Karachi 36.3°C
events.location: Mumbai, India and Karachi, Pakistan / South Asia Region
events.summary: Anomalously high temperatures continued to bake South Asia on October 28, with Mumbai recording a maximum of 35.6°C and Karachi reaching 36.3°C — both well above late-October climatological norms for the region. Pakistan's Meteorological Department forecast continued hot and dry conditions for Karachi with low humidity and northerly winds keeping relief at bay. This multi-day heat event follows prior reports of similar anomalies in Dhaka (36.7°C on October 27) and broadly reflects a persistent ridge of high pressure suppressing the normal seasonal cooling across South Asia.
